newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X CEO says confident of Busang reserve.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X CEO says confident of Busang reserve.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd chief executive David Walsh said on Thursday he is confident the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia has the reserve potential Bre-X has previously stated.

"We remain and have every confidence that there is the reserve potential in the Busang property that we have stated," Walsh told reporters at an impromptu news conference outside Bre-X's head office in Calgary.
Walsh also said it was "physically impossible" to tamper with core samples from the deposit. Walsh added he stands behind Bre-X's technical work on the Busang site.
Bre-X has estimated the Busang deposit contains 70.95 million ounces of gold, possibly one of the biggest gold finds of the century.

The mining world was stunned on Wednesday by Bre-X's admission that "there appears to be a strong possibility that the potential gold resources on the Busang project in East Kalimantan, Indonesia have been overstated because of invalid samples and assaying of those samples."
Freeport McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc Bre-X's partner in Busang, set off the alarm bells on Wednesday, saying that its own studies so far "indicate insignificant amounts of gold."
Bre-X's stock, which has been halted since Wednesday, is to resume trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange at 1500 EST/2000 GMT, the exchange said.
The stock, which traded a C$15.50 before it was halted, may sink as low as C$2 a share when trading resumes.
Walsh told reporters on Thursday that the company has drilled over 100 miles of core "and the assays have been consistent all the way through."
"It's physically impossible in our mind that the core could have been tampered with. You would have to have an army of people involved," he said.
Wednesday's shock came just one week after the mysterious death of Bre-X's chief Busang geologist, who fell out of a helicopter into the Borneo jungle in an apparent suicide.
Bre-X has hired Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd, an mining consultant, to conduct an audit of the drilling and sampling programs done by both Bre-X and Freeport.

"I stand behind that all the work that we've done technically has been done appropriately and like all the other trials and tribulations that we've gone through since discovering (Busang) that we'll be exonerated and the property will stand as we've indicated," Walsh said.
Walsh said his opinions were backed up by John Felderhof, Bre-X's head of exploration, who was in Jakarta on Thursday after returning from a visit of the Busang site.
